intro: Searching for a chartered surveyor near you usually means you have a property decision in front of you and want someone local who can look at it properly. Perhaps you are buying a home and want to know what condition it is really in, or you own a building and need a professional view on a problem. We can introduce you to a suitable UK surveyor in your area, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a local chartered surveyor usually need
need_lead: Most people typing this search want a qualified professional who can visit their property and give them a clear, independent view.
needs: You are buying a house and want a survey that goes further than the lender's basic valuation before you commit.
You have spotted cracking, damp or movement in a property you own and want to understand what is causing it and what to do next.
You are planning building work, an extension or a conversion and need advice on the structure and condition of the existing building.
You are dealing with a party wall matter with a neighbour and need a surveyor who works in that area.
You own or manage a property and want a professional assessment of its condition for maintenance or future planning.
context_heading: Chartered status and finding someone local
context: Chartered surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, using the letters MRICS or FRICS, and they follow RICS standards. RICS-regulated firms must hold insurance and offer a complaints process, so it is worth checking the RICS directory and asking whether the firm you speak to is regulated in that way.

Chartered status covers many specialisms, so a chartered surveyor near you may work in residential surveys, party wall matters, building defects or commercial property. Ask about their relevant experience for the specific job you have in mind, and confirm that the surveyor is independent of the sale if you are buying.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Tell us the type of property, such as a flat, a terraced house or an older building, and roughly when it was built if you know.
Explain what prompted the search, whether that is a purchase, a problem you have noticed or planned work.
Describe any specific concerns, such as damp, cracking, roof condition or a party wall issue.
Let us know your location so we can introduce you to a surveyor who covers your area.
Mention any deadline you are working towards, such as an exchange date or a contractor starting.
Say which type of report or advice you think you need, or ask us if you are unsure.
questions: Which type of survey or report are you recommending for this property, and what will it cover?
Are you independent of the sale and of any lender involved?
Is your firm regulated by RICS, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
What experience do you have with properties like mine and with the issue I have described?
Will you visit the property yourself, and who will carry out the inspection?
What is your fee, and what does it include?

faqs.q: What does chartered mean for a surveyor?
faqs.a: It means the surveyor is a member of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, using MRICS or FRICS, and follows RICS standards. RICS-regulated firms must also hold insurance and offer a complaints process.

faqs.q: Do I need a survey if my lender is arranging a valuation?
faqs.a: A lender's valuation is primarily for the lender's purposes and is not the same as a survey for you. A chartered surveyor can advise on the condition of the property and flag issues that matter to you as the buyer.

faqs.q: How do I judge which surveyor to choose?
faqs.a: Check the RICS directory, ask about their experience with your type of property and issue, and confirm which report type you are getting. Compare what each quote includes rather than price alone, and make sure the surveyor is independent of the sale.

faqs.q: Can a surveyor help with a party wall matter?
faqs.a: Yes, some surveyors specialise in party wall work, and there is a separate Faculty of Party Wall Surveyors for that area. Tell us about the dispute or notice so we can introduce you to someone with the right experience.
